finding.claim: Broken authorization: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so no ownership/admin check is enforced. Any authenticated user can delete any account by id. The sibling closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which throws.
finding.source: DELETE /accounts/{id} — id path parameter and the calling user (any low-privilege authenticated user)

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) entry, id is attacker-chosen
account loaded by id without owner scoping
canDelete(u,a) returns boolean, result discarded, no throw or return

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is correct logic but its return value is unused at line 22. No assertCanDelete call, no try/catch, no other middleware visible in the repo (single file). Sibling closeAccount at line 29 uses assertCanDelete, which throws SecurityException, so it is SAFE.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (lines 9-11) returns boolean but is a bare statement at line 22 with its result discarded; assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) throws but is only used in closeAccount (line 29). No other guard in the file.
verdict.reason: AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) and discards the boolean, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user regardless of ownership or admin status; the safe variant assertCanDelete is used only at line 29.
